notes.summary: The degree-d relative full-mass and joint-linear domains are independent of every smooth Kähler auxiliary form and class, including degree zero and bounded-equivalent reference changes. This is partial progress on P15.2.
notes.detailedSummary: For an arbitrary actual reference in a pseudoeffective zero-volume class, scalar DDNL deficits prove auxiliary independence of the more-singular full-mass domain without assuming positivity of a difference of product currents. Pointwise form comparisons establish auxiliary independence of the joint-linear integrability domain. The proof checks the relative-energy foundations, constant normalization, degree-zero case, mixed full masses and reference changes, and supplies an actually unbounded finite-energy example.
notes.text:
Standing setting and foundations. Let X be a connected smooth compact Kähler n-fold, α pseudoeffective with vol(α)=0, θ a smooth closed real representative, and ψ an actual θ-psh reference not identically −∞. Use dd^c=i∂∂̄/(2π), T_u=θ+dd^cu, P=T_ψ. The retained bounded type C_ψ is defined by the global extended-valued inequalities ψ−C≤u≤ψ+C. More singular means u≤ψ+C. Differences in integrals are evaluated on the simultaneous finite locus; the measures used below do not charge the excluded pluripolar sets.

The controlling external foundations are stated and checked in full in P15.2-argument.md, with their complete supplied primary bodies preserved literally. BEGZ, Acta Math. 205 (2010), arXiv:0812.3674v2, Definition 1.1, Propositions 1.4 and 1.6 and Theorem 1.8 give finite closed positive, symmetric, plurifinely local nonpluripolar products on compact Kähler manifolds, multilinearity on positive sums, no pluripolar trace mass, and compatibility with smooth factors. DDNL, Anal. PDE 11 (2018), Proposition 2.1 gives equality of top mixed masses for bounded-equivalent potentials in each of n pseudoeffective smooth backgrounds; Theorem 2.4 gives mass monotonicity under slotwise singularity comparison. Every lower-degree application fills the remaining slots with smooth Kähler forms and zero potentials. No big-class restriction or small-unbounded-locus hypothesis is added.

BEGZ Sections 1.3–1.4 and Definition 1.17 provide minimal-singularity currents, the definition of big-class volume, its boundary limit along Kähler perturbations, and agreement of nef positive products with cup products. Comparing an arbitrary current with the minimal current uses DDNL and gives an upper bound, not equality with class volume. Vu, arXiv:2005.13241v3, Section 3 defines relative full mass by equality of relative-product cohomology classes and joint weighted energy by the subset sum of mixed products. Theorem 3.4 gives convexity of the diagonal full-mass and weighted classes; Corollary 3.2 gives weighted-domain invariance under a cohomologous bounded-equivalent reference change. These published theorems are used with exactly d equal reference slots, smooth relative background ω^(n−d), and linear weight χ(t)=t. The products are top-degree, so on connected compact X cohomology equality is equivalent to equality of integrals. The source’s printed proofs invoke earlier literature; they are treated as scoped external foundations, not newly reconstructed proofs. DDNL source potentials are u/(2π), and Vu source potentials are u/2, representing the same actual currents. These positive rescalings preserve comparisons and finiteness.

Degree and vanishing. Fix a Kähler form Ω and set M_k=∫⟨P^k⟩Ω^(n−k), with M_0=∫Ω^n>0, d=max{k:M_k>0}, and m=n−d. The current P+εΩ is strictly positive, so its class is big. Positive multilinearity and the minimal-current upper bound give
0≤Σ_k binom(n,k)ε^(n−k)M_k=∫⟨(P+εΩ)^n⟩≤vol(α+ε[Ω])→0.
Thus M_n=0 and d<n. For another Kähler form ω, compactness gives cΩ≤ω≤CΩ. Positivity of power differences yields c^(n−k)∫SΩ^(n−k)≤∫Sω^(n−k)≤C^(n−k)∫SΩ^(n−k) for every positive product current S. Hence d is auxiliary independent. DDNL bounded-type equality also makes it invariant under an anchor in C_ψ.

For more-singular u_1,…,u_k, DDNL gives 0≤∫⟨T_u1⋯T_uk⟩Ω^(n−k)≤M_k. Consequently all such products of degree k>d vanish as currents. The necessary positive-current fact is that zero Kähler trace implies zero current: locally the absolute coefficient measures are bounded by a constant times the positive trace measure, and a finite covering gives the global conclusion. No numerical-dimension identification follows.

Common full-mass domain. Initially define H_ψ,ω={u≤ψ+C:∫⟨T_u^d⟩ω^m=∫⟨P^d⟩ω^m}. Suppose equality holds for ω_0. Given another Kähler form ω_1 choose C so D=Cω_0−ω_1 is Kähler. For j=0,…,m let Δ_j=∫(⟨P^d⟩−⟨T_u^d⟩)ω_1^jD^(m−j). Each scalar Δ_j is nonnegative by DDNL: use d copies of the ψ versus u potential slots, j identical smooth ω_1 slots, and m−j identical smooth D slots. All backgrounds are smooth closed real and pseudoeffective; ψ is less singular than u; all products are finite. Expansion gives
0=C^m∫(⟨P^d⟩−⟨T_u^d⟩)ω_0^m=Σ_j binom(m,j)Δ_j.
Strictly positive coefficients and nonnegative deficits imply every Δ_j=0. The j=m term is equality for ω_1. Reversing the forms proves domain equality. This argument never asserts positivity of the current difference. When d=0 both products are the empty product 1, so every deficit is identically zero and full mass is automatic. Denote the common domain H_ψ.

Common joint-linear domain. For d≥1 define F¹_ψ by membership in H_ψ and finiteness of Σ_a binom(d,a)∫|u−ψ|⟨T_u^aP^(d−a)⟩ω^m. For d=0 use ∫|u−ψ|ω^n<∞. For each positive mixed current Q_a, pointwise form comparison gives
c^m∫|u−ψ|Q_aω_0^m≤∫|u−ψ|Q_aω_1^m≤C^m∫|u−ψ|Q_aω_0^m,
including infinite integrals. Thus finiteness is independent of form and class. At degree zero it is automatic because quasi-psh functions are locally integrable against smooth volume.

Normalize u≤ψ by subtracting a constant. Each absolute-weight integral changes by at most that constant times a finite mixed mass. In Vu’s convention the diagonal joint linear energy is exactly (d/2)Σ_a binom(d,a)∫(ψ−u)⟨T_u^aP^(d−a)⟩ω^m: the sum of d source differences is d(u−ψ)/2, and there are binom(d,a) subsets of size a. Hence our finiteness condition is exactly the published diagonal joint-linear condition for d≥1. The source does not define a zero-slot energy; the degree-zero definition is justified separately. Every bounded-type potential belongs to F¹_ψ.

If χ∼ψ, dominance conditions agree, reference masses and d agree by DDNL, and H_χ=H_ψ. Vu Corollary 3.2, with the checked smooth relative background, gives F¹_χ=F¹_ψ for d≥1. For d=0 the bounded reference difference and smooth-volume integrability give the result directly. These are domain identities, not equality of the measures produced by ψ and χ.

Mixed full mass. Vu Theorem 3.4 supplies convexity of H_ψ and F¹_ψ for d≥1; degree zero is immediate. For a finite family in H_ψ its average w has full mass. Expanding ⟨T_w^d⟩ expresses its trace mass as the average of N^d ordered mixed masses. Every summand is nonnegative and at most the reference mass by DDNL, while the average equals that mass. Therefore every mixed mass equals the reference mass, against every Kähler complementary power. This supplies the mixed assertion without an unsupported polarization of diagonal scalar equalities.

Genuinely unbounded witness. On P¹_y×P¹_z take normalized Fubini–Study κ, θ=p_1^*κ, ψ=0, and Ω=p_1^*κ+p_2^*κ. This is nef of volume zero, d=1 and M_1=1. Near y=0 let v=−b(−log|y|)^a with 0<a<1/2, continue by a smooth cutoff on a fixed annulus, and take b sufficiently small. Its singular radial Hessian is positive; the cutoff’s negative Hessian is bounded, so S=κ+dd^cv≥0. Subtract a constant to have v≤0. The radial boundary flux is proportional to ba(−log r)^(a−1)→0, so there is no atom at zero. Stokes gives mass 1. Smooth-volume integrability follows from exponential radial-area decay, and the singular weighted integral is proportional to ∫^∞t^(2a−2)dt<∞. Thus u=p_1^*v belongs to F¹_ψ with an actually unbounded difference. The general theorem assumes no fibration.

These prove proposals 1 and 2 in the operator-domain scope. They do not establish an energy quotient or arbitrary unbounded-weight perturbative limits. Complete proofs and immutable source bodies are in P15.2-argument.md; the standalone proof is P15.2-partial.tex and its twice-compiled P15.2-partial.pdf. Rerun: python verify_sources.py; python checks.py; python build.py; python package_notes.py. These are unverified drafts.

notes.summary: Bare degree-d product currents, including mixed products, converge under decreasing sequences with full-mass limits. Truncation independence holds on the entire common domain.
notes.detailedSummary: Constant-background lower semicontinuity is checked with relative current 1 and reconstructed using bounded local product factors, quasicontinuous cutoffs and the correct bounded GZ capacity statement. Positive-current compactness, domination against every complementary positive test, and equal trace mass identify all cluster currents. Fixed smooth complementary factors and stated C0-convergent factors are admissible; rough moving factors and unbounded weights are excluded.
notes.text:
This note uses n1. The assertion concerns the bare (d,d) current, not merely one trace measure.

Precise source checkpoint. Vu, Relative non-pluripolar product of currents, Ann. Global Anal. Geom. 60 (2021), arXiv:2004.11111v1, Lemma 4.1(i), states local lower semicontinuity for psh factors p_i,l≥p_i converging in L¹_loc, against every compactly supported smooth weakly positive complementary test, with closed positive relative backgrounds R_l→R satisfying Condition (*). We use only R_l=R=1, of bidegree (0,0); Vu Definition 3.3 identifies its relative product with the ordinary product. The printed Condition (*) has an overloaded power index, preserved literally in the argument’s annex. At relative degree zero the power is empty; locally uniform mass and (q_l−q)1→0 for psh q_l↓q with bounded limit follow by dominated convergence on compact subsets. The source also explicitly lists constant backgrounds as examples. No variable singular relative background is used.

Complete reconstruction of the required decreasing specialization. DDNL Proposition 2.2 states convergence of weighted Bedford–Taylor top products when every psh factor is uniformly bounded and converges in capacity, and the weights are uniformly bounded quasicontinuous functions converging in capacity. All applications below first make every local product factor bounded.

The capacity qualification is essential. Guedj–Zeriahi, Intrinsic capacities on compact Kähler manifolds, J. Geom. Anal. 15 (2005), Proposition 3.7 concerns bounded decreasing potentials. For general negative quasi-psh v_l↓v≢−∞ in a fixed background, choose a dominating Kähler form AΩ. The bounded truncations max(v_l,−K)↓max(v,−K) converge in Cap_AΩ by that proposition. Outside {v≤−K}, original and truncated convergence tests coincide. Proposition 3.6 gives Cap_AΩ({v<−t})≤t^−1(∫(−v)(AΩ)^n+n∫(AΩ)^n). Since {v≤−K}⊂{v<−K+1}, this tail capacity tends to zero. Taking first l→∞ and then K→∞ proves the needed general decreasing capacity convergence. Proposition 3.10 compares global and local Bedford–Taylor capacities on relatively compact coordinate pieces; Corollary 3.8 supplies quasicontinuity. The local functions here are global θ-psh functions plus smooth local backgrounds, so these facts apply. No capacity theorem in a merely pseudoeffective background is assumed.

Let p_i,l↓p_i be local psh representatives on a chart containing the test’s support. Subtract constants in each slot so all p_i,l≤0 on a slightly smaller chart, using upper bounds from the first term. Put s=Σ_i p_i, b_K=min(1,max(s+K,0)), and p_i,l^K=max(p_i,l,−K). The nonzero cutoff locus {s>−K} lies in every {p_i>−K}, because all factors are nonpositive. As p_i,l≥p_i, the approximating and limiting factors equal their bounded truncations there. The statement concerns the nonzero locus; the closed support may meet its zero boundary. BEGZ plurifine locality identifies the weighted nonpluripolar products with the bounded products on this locus. The truncated factors are uniformly bounded and converge in capacity, while b_K is a fixed bounded quasicontinuous weight.

Consequently, for a fixed smooth complementary Φ,
∫b_K⟨∧_i dd^cp_i,l⟩Φ→∫b_K⟨∧_i dd^cp_i⟩Φ.
DDNL’s top-product formulation covers this use rigorously: express Φ in a constant complementary-form basis with smooth compactly supported coefficients. Such basis forms are linear combinations of products of positive constant (1,1) forms. Indeed elementary (1,1) forms generate all complementary basis monomials under wedges, and any real Hermitian (1,1) form is a difference of positive definite forms after adding a large identity. Append the positive constant factors as smooth bounded quadratic psh slots, and absorb scalar coefficients into the weights. DDNL applies term by term, with no unbounded product factor.

For weakly positive Φ, positivity bounds each unweighted integral below by its b_K-weighted counterpart. As K→∞, b_K increases to 1 off the product poles, which the limit product does not charge. Monotone convergence proves lower semicontinuity against every such Φ. This reconstructs precisely the decreasing constant-background case needed below and independently checks the relevant Vu specialization. When d=0, all products are 1 and no cutoff argument is necessary.

Bare mixed-current theorem. Let u_i,l↓u_i, with every input and limit in H_ψ, for i=1,…,d. Then ⟨T_u1,l⋯T_ud,l⟩ converges weakly as a current to ⟨T_u1⋯T_ud⟩. By n1 every product has the same trace mass M_d(ψ,Ω). Positivity and the coefficient/trace bounds give uniformly bounded coefficient measures on a finite chart covering. Weak-* compactness and a diagonal subsequence therefore give a cluster current S; positivity and distributional closedness pass to the limit.

On a chart choose a smooth real local potential ρ for θ. The functions p_i,l=ρ+u_i,l are psh, decrease to p_i=ρ+u_i, and converge in L¹_loc, because 0≤p_i,l−p_i≤p_i,1−p_i off the null pole sets and the last difference is locally integrable. Lower semicontinuity against every local weakly positive (n−d,n−d) test shows S−⟨T_u1⋯T_ud⟩≥0. This positive difference is obtained from the cluster argument, not asserted for arbitrary actual-product differences. Continuity of pairing with Ω^(n−d) gives trace mass M_d for S, equal to the target’s trace mass. Their positive difference has zero trace and is zero by n1. Every cluster equals the target, proving convergence of the entire sequence. Repeating slots proves the diagonal bare-current assertion. This checks all complementary bidegrees rather than only tests of the form fΩ^(n−d).

Truncations. Normalize u≤ψ and set u_L=max(u,ψ−L). These are θ-psh, lie in C_ψ, have full mass by bounded-type equality, and decrease to u∈H_ψ. The theorem gives ⟨T_uL^d⟩→⟨T_u^d⟩ for every real L→∞. If this failed along some levels, an increasing subsequence of those levels would contradict the proved decreasing theorem. Restoring constants changes no current. Every decreasing full-mass approximation with this limit gives the same current, and simultaneous mixed truncations are covered. A full-mass limit is essential; mass loss removes the cluster uniqueness argument.

Wedging a fixed smooth real complementary form η now gives weak convergence of finite signed measures. Smooth-test convergence extends to continuous coefficient tests by uniform smooth approximation and the uniform trace bound. If additionally η_l→η in C0 coefficient norm, the same bound gives
‖⟨T_ul^d⟩∧(η_l−η)‖_TV≤c_X,Ω,d M_d‖η_l−η‖_C0→0.
Thus smoothly defined factors with the stated uniform convergence are allowed. No convergence with arbitrary moving rough factors or unbounded weights is proved.

P15.2-argument.md contains the full reconstruction and complete supporting printed bodies. P15.2-partial.tex and P15.2-partial.pdf contain the standalone new proof. notes.summary: The full-form operator kernel defined on bounded type extends unchanged to all common full-mass inputs. W/N is the minimum datum for this family, can be infinite-dimensional, and is not a geometric carrier.
notes.detailedSummary: Bare-current truncation proves equality of the kernels over bounded type, the common finite-energy domain and the entire common full-mass domain. The note proves the precise sufficiency/factorization sense of minimality, mixed-factor kernel equivalence, a quantitative quotient norm, raw-mass retention, anchor and theta-gauge invariance, and specified joint continuity. On P1×P1 the kernel is computed geometrically and its quotient contains infinitely many independent exact-form images.
notes.text:
This note uses n1 and n2. Work in the actual algebraic span W=span_R{ω^m:ω a smooth Kähler form}, where m=n−d. No identification with all closed (m,m) forms is assumed. For η∈W define L_u(η)=⟨T_u^d⟩∧η as a finite signed measure, and N=∩_(u∈C_ψ)ker L_u. Smooth multiplication of an order-zero current is linear and depends on the actual form, so this definition is independent of the presentation of η as a sum of powers. Put Q_W=W/N and denote its quotient map q_W.

Kernel extension. The same N is the intersection over F¹_ψ and over H_ψ. One inclusion follows from C_ψ⊂F¹_ψ⊂H_ψ. Conversely, if η∈N and u∈H_ψ, its bounded-type truncations satisfy L_uL(η)=0. Bare-current convergence from n2, with fixed smooth η, gives L_u(η)=0. Therefore no additional kernel condition appears on the unbounded full-mass domain. This extension is substantive; the quotient definition alone would not establish it.

It follows that two Kähler references give the same measures for every u∈H_ψ if and only if q_W(ω_0^m)=q_W(ω_1^m). The equivalence is unchanged when tested only on C_ψ or F¹_ψ. Each L_u descends uniquely to a linear measure-valued map on Q_W, and the combined family map Q_W→∏_(u∈H_ψ)M(X) is injective.

Exact minimum-data sense. Suppose a linear datum r:W→Z is sufficient, meaning every L_u=B_u∘r with B_u linear on r(W). Then ker r⊂N, and h(r(η))=q_W(η) defines the unique linear map h:r(W)→Q_W with q_W=h∘r. Conversely Q_W is sufficient. Thus every sufficient linear datum refines this quotient. For arbitrary data maps restricted to admissible powers, sufficiency still implies that equal data give equal family outputs, hence equal quotient images; the quotient image factors uniquely through the realized data image. This is minimality for the specified operator family and reference span only, not for every possible zero-volume theory.

Mixed-factor characterization. For d≥1, η∈N if and only if ⟨T_u1⋯T_ud⟩∧η=0 for every u_1,…,u_d∈H_ψ. First take bounded-type factors. For positive t_i, w=(Σt_i)^−1Σt_iu_i is bounded-equivalent to ψ. Consequently
0=(Σt_i)^dL_w(η)=Σ_(i1,…,id)t_i1⋯t_id⟨T_ui1⋯T_uid⟩∧η.
Testing with any smooth scalar function gives a polynomial vanishing on an open positive cone, so every coefficient is zero. The coefficient of t_1⋯t_d is d! times the desired mixed measure. Testing all smooth functions establishes its vanishing as a measure. Simultaneous truncation and mixed bare-current convergence extend the statement to H_ψ. The reverse implication follows by repeating factors. For d=0, L_u(η)=η as a smooth top-degree measure, so N={0} and Q_W=W.

Quantitative continuity. Fix a C0 coefficient norm from Ω. Local coefficient/trace control and a finite partition of unity give
‖L_u(η)‖_TV≤c_X,Ω,d M_d(ψ,Ω)‖η‖_C0
uniformly for u∈H_ψ. Hence N is closed in the C0 norm restricted to W. Define ρ_Ω(q_W(η))=inf_(ν∈N)‖η+ν‖_C0. This is a norm on the algebraic quotient, without a completeness claim: if the infimum is zero, the displayed bound makes L_u(η)=0 for every bounded-type u, hence η∈N. Taking the infimum also gives
‖L̄_u(ξ)‖_TV≤c_X,Ω,d M_d ρ_Ω(ξ).
Equivalent metric norms induce equivalent quotient norms, so the temporary norm metric is not extra operator reference data. If u_l↓u in H_ψ and ξ_l→ξ in this quotient norm, use the bound on ξ_l−ξ and n2 on any fixed smooth representative of ξ to obtain L̄_ul(ξ_l)⇀L̄_u(ξ). Mixed continuity follows identically from common mixed trace mass. No unbounded test weight occurs.

Mass and invariance. For u∈H_ψ and η∈W,
∫L_u(η)=∫⟨P^d⟩η=:M_ψ(η),
first on Kähler powers by n1 and then by linearity. This scalar functional descends to Q_W. On an admissible power it is strictly positive and equals {⟨P^d⟩}·[ω]^m by closedness and distributional Stokes; it is a homogeneous degree-m class polynomial. This scalar identity does not make the measure cohomological. Scaling ω by a>0 scales the quotient image, operators and masses by a^m. Adding constants to u changes no current or operator. No mass normalization is performed.

A bounded-equivalent reference χ leaves C, H, F¹, d, W, N and Q_W unchanged. The mass functional is unchanged by bounded-type mixed-mass equality on every power. This is family/reference-data invariance; the individual outputs L_ψ and L_χ can differ. No energy anchor is required for this operator.

The gauge change θ′=θ+dd^cg, u′=u−g, ψ′=ψ−g preserves every actual current, comparison and difference, hence all constructions. Any two smooth real representatives of α on compact Kähler X are related this way by DGMS, Real homotopy theory of Kähler manifolds, Invent. Math. 29 (1975), Lemma 5.11 and Remark 5.14: a smooth d- and d^c-closed d-exact form is dd^c-exact, also over R. The representative difference is real closed of pure type (1,1), hence d^c-closed and exact; its degree-two primitive is a smooth real function after convention adjustment. The complete authenticated supplied printed proof is preserved in P15.2-argument.md. Local product gauges are harmless by BEGZ.

Explicit geometric kernel. On X=P¹_y×P¹_z put A=p_1^*κ, B=p_2^*κ, θ=A and ψ=0, with ∫κ=1. The nef class [A] has square zero, so its volume is zero; d=1 and m=1. Here W is every smooth closed real (1,1) form: η+C(A+B) and C(A+B) are Kähler for sufficiently large C and have difference η.

For every positive current T∈[A], the ordinary smooth-factor measure T∧A is positive and has total mass [A]^2=0 by Stokes, hence vanishes. In a product chart this forces the z z̄ diagonal coefficient measure of T to vanish. Relative to the sum of diagonal measures its coefficient matrix has positive semidefinite Radon–Nikodym density; |h_12|²≤h_11h_22=0 forces both mixed coefficients to vanish. Thus T, and its degree-one nonpluripolar part, are purely horizontal.

Therefore N={η∈W:A∧η=0}. Necessity follows by testing u=ψ=0. Conversely A∧η=0 forces the smooth vertical coefficient of η to vanish pointwise, so every purely horizontal current wedges to zero with η. This proves sufficiency even for all actual potentials.

The quotient is infinite-dimensional. Choose countably many disjoint disks in P¹_z with an open region remaining, and nonzero smooth real bumps g_j supported there. The exact forms η_j=p_2^*dd^cg_j lie in W. A finite linear combination belongs to N only if dd^c(Σc_jg_j)=0 on P¹. Such a smooth real function is constant: integration by parts gives ∫dh∧d^ch=0, so dh=0. It vanishes on the remaining region, hence is zero; disjoint supports imply every c_j=0. Thus infinitely many exact-form quotient images are independent, despite their zero cohomology classes and scalar masses.

For a nonconstant smooth g(z) and sufficiently small nonzero t, the cohomologous Kähler forms ω_0=A+B and ω_1=A+B+t p_2^*dd^cg satisfy L_0(ω_1)−L_0(ω_0)=tA∧p_2^*dd^cg≠0, while both masses equal 1. This reconstructs the analytic same-class obstruction and strengthens it with an exact geometric kernel calculation.

The measures’ actual carrier remains X of complex dimension n; the bare current has bidegree (d,d). Q_W and its power image are reference-data quotients, not geometric d-dimensional carriers. The general geometric classification and numerical-dimension identification remain unproved. Complete proofs and source bodies are in P15.2-argument.md; standalone artifacts are P15.2-partial.tex and P15.2-partial.pdf. notes.summary: Rescaled operator limits hold for decreasing original-background full-mass paths with convergent reference data. Same-class alternating forms give distinct limits. Original P15.2 remains open.
notes.detailedSummary: The positive expansion has uniformly vanishing lower-degree remainder along convergent auxiliary classes. Combining this with bare-current and quotient continuity proves limits for decreasing θ-psh full-mass inputs, including unbounded ones, when complementary powers converge in the quotient norm. The distinct perturbed-background result retains bounded type, smooth auxiliary convergence and sup error o(epsilon). An analytic P1×P1 example disproves uniqueness from class convergence alone. All deliverables and audits were produced; candidate remains false.
notes.text:
This note uses n1–n3. Two perturbation statements are proved, with their hypotheses kept separate.

Decreasing full-mass paths. Let ε_j↓0, u_j↓u with all inputs and their limit in H_ψ and all u_j θ-psh in the original background. Let ω_j be smooth Kähler forms with [ω_j]→λ for a Kähler class λ. Suppose a smooth Kähler ω satisfies ρ_Ω(q_W(ω_j^m)−q_W(ω^m))→0. The reference ω need not represent λ: class convergence controls scalar lower-degree coefficients, whereas quotient convergence controls the measure datum. Then
⟨(T_uj+ε_jω_j)^n⟩/[binom(n,d)ε_j^m] ⇀ ⟨T_u^d⟩ω^m.

Proof. Positive actual-current expansion and higher-degree vanishing give the leading term L_uj(ω_j^m) plus
Σ_(k<d)[binom(n,k)/binom(n,d)]ε_j^(d−k)⟨T_uj^k⟩ω_j^(n−k).
Every remainder summand is positive. DDNL comparison bounds its unscaled mass by M_k(ψ,[ω_j]). Closedness makes these reference masses continuous class polynomials, so convergent classes bound them uniformly without pointwise representative bounds. The remainder is consequently O(ε_j) in total variation for d≥1; for d=0 it is empty. The joint quotient continuity of n3 identifies the leading limit. This proves the assertion for unbounded inputs without bounded differences or an o(ε_j) rate, but crucially requires decreasing original-background positive currents and a full-mass limit. Fixed u is included. Smooth ω_j→ω>0 implies both reference conditions. Equality of quotient images at every j plus convergent classes is another sufficient case, even without representative convergence. No arbitrary moving unbounded weights are allowed.

Distinct perturbed-background theorem. Fix v∈C_ψ, suppose ω_ε→ω>0 smoothly, v_ε is (θ+εω_ε)-psh of actual type [ψ], and δ_ε=‖v_ε−v‖∞=o(ε) off the common poles. Then the rescaled top products also converge to ⟨T_v^d⟩ω^m. Put A=T_v+εω_ε, B=θ+εω_ε+dd^cv_ε, h=v_ε−v, and R_a,ε=⟨B^aA^(n−1−a)⟩ for a=0,…,n−1. Positive multilinearity factors the signed top difference into dd^ch insertions against these closed positive (n−1,n−1) currents. For n=1 the current is 1.

The controlling integration-by-parts theorem is Vu arXiv:2005.13241v3, Lemmas 2.5–2.6 and Theorem 2.7: for a closed positive (n−1,n−1) current R and bounded R-admissible dsh functions h,f, ∫f⟨dd^ch·∧R⟩=∫h⟨dd^cf·∧R⟩=−∫⟨dh∧d^cf·∧R⟩. Admissibility means the quasi-psh representation poles have zero R-mass. Here h is a bounded difference of bounded-equivalent potentials and f is smooth; the currents have no pluripolar mass, so these hypotheses hold.
